primitives.name: Elo Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: We adapted the proven Elo rating system to develop player ratings that evaluate game performance while also accounting for strength of opponent.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that game outcomes are probabilistic functions of the difference in skill ratings between players and opponents, with higher-rated players having a higher probability of winning.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Does not handle simultaneous multi-player interactions or non-zero-sum scenarios directly.

layer2.mapping: Maps player performance evaluation to conformal prediction intervals in GSI for uncertainty quantification, and to Markov decision processes in GSE for sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error reduction in NFL performance projections compared to baseline models.

primitives.name: Performance Curve
primitives.verbatim_quote: We use our player performance curves as the basis for projecting NFL potential.
primitives.assumptions: Suggests that an individual player's career trajectory follows a smooth, predictable function over time, allowing for linear interpolation or extrapolation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: May break down during injury, rule changes, or sudden coaching staff alterations.

layer2.mapping: Represents state-transition dynamics in GSE where performance curves map current states to future action spaces, and serves as prior distributions in GSI for Bayesian updating of player prospects.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation coefficient between projected and actual NFL career completion rates.

primitives.name: Opponent Adjustment
primitives.verbatim_quote: brian.lehman@visionistinc.com Abstract Everyone attempts to determine which college football players will succeed at the next level.
primitives.assumptions: Adjusts raw performance metrics by the Elo ratings of opposing defenses, normalizing for varying difficulty of competition faced across different college programs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when opponent quality is poorly estimated due to small sample sizes or roster turnover.

layer2.mapping: Derives conditional probability kernels for GSE transition matrices given defensive strength, and provides robust likelihood adjustments in GSI hierarchical models.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement in predictive accuracy when cross-validated against unseen NFL seasons.

primitives.name: Development Limitation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Introduction At last year's conference, Mike Leach offered his opinion on the belief that an inaccurate college athlete can be developed into an NFL quarterback, simply stating, "You can't coach accuracy."1 The selection of a great franchise quarterback can be dramatic.
primitives.assumptions: Establishes an upper bound on player improvement based on inherent physical attributes and foundational skills that are difficult to alter through training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when external factors like coaching innovation or rule changes significantly alter the required skill set.

layer2.mapping: Maps to capacity constraints in GSE reinforcement learning algorithms and to prior variance inflation in GSI predictive intervals for ceiling effects.
layer2.telemetry: R-squared decrease in regression models when attempting to predict extreme performance improvements.
